messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER — Production alert: 90th/95th token latency spike on streaming responses (hosted-usw2, hosted-eu). Error rate 502/504 upstream increasing. Root TS: 1910005678

maria (oncall): acknowledged, I'm on it. pulling traces and recent deploys. any customer-facing alerts yet?

sam (eng-runtime): I see increased tail latency on grpc-to-runtime and a backlog in the streaming worker queues. Non-stream paths look less impacted.

lee (sre): CPU on shared streaming pool nodes jumped ~3x starting ~1910005400. Autoscale didn't react fast enough. could be a pathological set of long-lived streams.

maria (oncall): ok. plan: 1) reduce acceptance of new streaming connections (throttle), 2) if that doesn't reduce queue we toggle streaming responses off for hosted tier while we stabilize, 3) notify support. agree?

sam (eng-runtime): yes. I can push a traffic-shaping rule to drop new streaming handshakes for low-tier keys and rate-limit for others. command ready: 
```
# apply temporary streaming throttle
curl -X POST "https://admin.internal/api/v1/traffic-shaping" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"rule":"stream_new_conn","mode":"throttle","rate_per_minute":20,"targets":["free","trial"]}'
```

sam (eng-runtime): I'm applying that now to prod-usw2 and prod-eu.

sam (eng-runtime): applied to usw2 and eu-west. metrics should update in ~30s.

lee (sre): seeing incoming streaming handshake rate drop ~60% for free/trial. queue depth down ~25%. tail latency still elevated but trending down.

karen (support): Heads up — I'm drafting a customer note for affected customers (free/trial tiers). Want to include estimated ETA for full restoration.

maria (oncall): give it 10m after throttle. if 95th latency not < target (400ms) we'll flip streaming off for hosted API and serve non-streaming (poll/paginated) fallback.

[10 minutes pass]

lee (sre): throttle helped but not enough. 95th still ~1.2s in eu, and several long-lived streams still consuming memory. Auto-recovery risks. recommend temporary disable.

sam (eng-runtime): prepared feature-flag toggle. Two-step safe path: 1) set flag so new responses default to non-streaming, 2) set global ingress policy to reject streaming SSE upgrade handshake (graceful). Command: 
```
# disable streaming responses quickly
curl -X POST "https://admin.internal/api/v1/feature_flags/streaming_responses" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"enabled":false,"scope":"hosted","reason":"latency_mitigation","ticket":"INC-1910"}'
```

sam (eng-runtime): I'll also add a canary to fileserver so control plane sees no regressions. rolling out to 10% first.

maria (oncall): do it. document rollback steps in the change comment. support will send notice to impacted customers as soon as canary is green.

sam (eng-runtime): canary rollout in progress. logs: 
```
[INFO] rollouts: streaming_responses flag -> disabled (canary 10%)\n[INFO] route update pushed to gateway-canary pods
```

lee (sre): monitoring shows worker memory usage stabilizing on canary nodes. latency on canary paths down to 280ms 95th.

sam (eng-runtime): canary looks good. promoting to 100% now. applying ingress rejection for SSE upgrade to avoid half-open streams: 
```
kubectl -n gateway-prod patch configmap gateway-ingress --patch '{"data":{"sse_upgrade":"reject"}}'
```

maria (oncall): done?

sam (eng-runtime): done. streaming responses disabled for hosted customers. non-streaming fallback returned to clients.

karen (support): sent customer message to known integrators and active trial accounts: short note with workaround (switch to poll modes or increase chunk window). initial replies: two customers confirming they can switch; one reported degraded UX.

maria (oncall): incidents: immediate customer impact = streaming clients see aborted streams and fall back to non-streaming behavior. Severity: S2 for us, S3 for a few enterprise customers (we're monitoring).

lee (sre): taking mitigations: scaled dedicated streaming pool to +30% (for customers on Dedicated plan) to reduce collision risk once we re-enable. also working on kernel timeouts for long-lived streams.

sam (eng-runtime): set a temporary global max-stream-duration=10m to prevent runaway connections when we re-enable. diff: 
```
# config snippet
max_stream_duration: 600 # seconds
stream_handshake_timeout: 10
```

maria (oncall): good. timeline: disabled streaming at 1910005860. we'll hold disabled state while we: 1) drain long-lived connections, 2) fix autoscaler bug for streaming pool, 3) roll out improved rate-limiter. target re-enable in 4-8 hours depending on testing.

karen (support): publishing status page entry now and linking to workaround. include ETA window and contact for enterprise accounts.

sam (eng-runtime): filing an action ticket with runbook updates and rollback steps: INC-1910. will include exact admin commands and observability dashboards.

maria (oncall): handing off to lee for overnight stabilization. I'll do a quick post-incident note and then pass to on-call night. 

lee (sre): acknowledged. I'll continue monitoring latency and queue depth, keep paging threshold lowered. If we see error rate fall below baseline for 30m and autoscaler validated, we'll coordinate a soft re-enable (canary -> 10% -> 100%) during low-traffic window.

maria (oncall): thanks team. summary for handoff: streaming disabled for hosted at 1910005860, mitigations applied (throttle -> disable), support notified, dedicated pool scaled, follow-up tickets: INC-1910 (root cause + autoscaler fix), OPS-1234 (streaming runbook). I'm logging everything to the incident doc. :white_check_mark: 

karen (support): oncall handoff note posted in #support-ops with link to status page.

incident-bot: Incident INC-1910 assigned to lee. Next on-call: night@redwood.

lee (sre): taking over. will update thread with next check-in at +30m or sooner on regressions.

[end thread]
